name_zh: 佩龙-弗罗贝尼乌斯定理
canonical_name: Perron-Frobenius spectral theorem family for finite nonnegative matrices
statement_blocker: The catalog supplies only 'spectral properties of nonnegative matrices'. It does not select an arbitrary, irreducible, primitive, or strictly positive matrix theorem; fix the scalar field and finite index type; or choose the Perron-root, eigenvector, simplicity, dominance, peripheral-spectrum, normalization, and degenerate-case clauses. Perron's 1907 source lead and Frobenius's later extensions are not yet reconciled or independently reviewed. Choosing an exact proposition at intake would invent, broaden, narrow, or substitute mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: an approved source must fix a finite square index type and nonemptiness/dimension convention, the real or complex scalar encoding, entrywise order, and every structure needed for spectrum and multiplicity.
conclusion: Open: the repository does not choose the existence/sign/eigenvector core for arbitrary nonnegative matrices, the stronger irreducible conclusion, the primitive or strictly positive strict-dominance theorem, or a peripheral-spectrum classification.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before a proposition is selected; the statement phase must resolve every boundary case listed in scope-map.md.
candidate_scope_not_credited: every finite entrywise-nonnegative real matrix has its spectral radius as an eigenvalue with a nonzero nonnegative right eigenvector
every finite irreducible nonnegative real matrix has a positive simple Perron root and positive eigenvector, with weak modulus dominance
every finite primitive or strictly positive real matrix has a unique positive Perron root with strict modulus dominance
the peripheral eigenvalues of an irreducible nonnegative matrix form a source-specified cyclic family
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: empty, singleton, and zero-dimensional index types
zero, identity, diagonal, reducible, and block-triangular matrices
irreducible periodic but imprimitive matrices and tied peripheral moduli
primitive, strictly positive, stochastic, permutation, and symmetric special cases
left versus right eigenvectors and real versus complex spectrum
algebraic versus geometric simplicity and repeated roots
normalization and uniqueness up to positive scaling
excluded_substitutions: the out-of-scope positive-matrix physics record THM-P-0887
generic spectral-radius attainment without a nonnegative Perron eigenvector
generic eigenvalue existence over an algebraically closed field
irreducibility, primitivity, graph connectivity, or positive matrix-power characterizations alone
Cayley-Hamilton, Schur decomposition, Jordan form, Gershgorin bounds, or the spectral theorem
stochastic-only, symmetric-only, fixed-dimension, reducible-only, or numerical special cases
a structure or hypothesis storing the desired Perron eigenvalue, eigenvector, simplicity, or dominance conclusion
the catalog's untrusted verified label or the discovery probe as source or proof credit
